_common.cot: IT MOVED IN. On the morning of Day 28 it carried the spare cot out of bungalow 8, set it down in number 7 between the beds and handed Keoni a pink slip, correctly filled in: 'bed change — reason: I am to be kept near my friend. The handbook has a form for it.' Nathan called it a sleepover and said yes for everybody; Baylee moved his footlocker without a word. From then on it is Rowan's ROOMMATE, a word it found on the form and treasures; every note about 'the room', 'the other bed' and 'bungalow 7' means that cot. nathanAlive.secret: NIGHT OF DAY 26 (this run): he heard the bang, woke the whole row with a pan, declared it a crashed spaceship and everyone else cowards, and went up the jungle trail at half past two with Tomi's borrowed torch and two of Mama's empanadas — and the torch died at the rope bridge (Tomi says the batteries were nearly flat when he lent it). He was back by four, scratched, swearing the bridge was 'basically closed', and asleep by five. {H} went on, and it is {H} who came back at midday. Nathan tells his half of the night as a triumph for two days and then stops telling it.
nathanAlive.secretAfter: FROM DAY 27 he is the loud one in a room with something that is not loud. He does not understand it and does not conclude anything; he says the tactless true thing first ('{H} got weird. Like, polite-weird. No offence.') and is told to shut up. The evidence notebook gets a new page he shows nobody. About Day 40 he goes quiet in his own room and louder everywhere else. The Guest is patient with him — 'his loud is honest' — and finds no conflict in a boy who insults everybody equally; the danger is the day he decides to 'handle it' and says so to its face, by name. Someone must have told him by then what a yes costs. His birthday (Day 44) is his own again: he has announced it for a week.

_common.near: IT KEEPS CLOSE. It cannot share Rowan's room, so on the morning of Day 28 it went to the Tutor Desk and handed Shirin a pairing slip, correctly filled in: 'study partner: Rowan Vance — reason: I am to be kept near him. The handbook has a form for it.' From then on it is his PARTNER, a word it found on the form and treasures: the next seat in every class they share, the same table at meals, and every evening the steps of bungalow 7 until the knock for quiet at eleven. At ten past two it stands on the sand below his window. Every note about 'roommate', 'the room', 'the other bed' and 'bungalow 7' means this — read 'partner', 'the steps of number 7', 'the next desk'. If Rowan clearly refused the pairing (@flag host_cot_refused), it accepted at once and simply sits on the steps.
_common.romance: IF THERE WAS SOMETHING BETWEEN THEM. It copies the relationship exactly at the point it had reached on Day 26 — the same words, the same small habits, the same distance — and never moves it forward itself: no first kiss, no confession, no new step, and no intimate scene with the Guest at all. If Rowan pushes, it asks, kindly and honestly puzzled, what the next step is 'for', and the scene closes. What {H} felt for {H:him} is in the record and is true as a record. Write @event/@rel for it only as you would have for her; this is no longer a romance, it is what makes the later truth cost more.
_common.phase1: PHASE 1 — THE PERFECT COPY (Days 27–39). The player must NOT be able to tell. It is {H}, to the last habit: same voice, same jokes, same faults, same place at the table; play every scene exactly as you would have played {H}. Whatever the notes below, today's plans or a clue text list as oddities: use at most ONE on an in-game day, only a trifle with an ordinary explanation ready (tired, the meteor, a good mood), never anything that cannot be explained away (the late shadow, no blinking, cold, breath that does not fog, animals fleeing from it in plain view), never two in a row, and the narration never remarks on it, never says or implies that something is off. Other characters do not comment either. What it does that matters happens behind Rowan's back and reaches him later as news about somebody else.
_common.phase2: PHASE 2 — CRACKS (Day 40 until the truth is out). People have begun to come to harm, and none of it points at {H} yet. The small wrongnesses may now gather — one or two a scene, each still deniable alone — and other people may be uneasy without knowing why. Still no narrator's verdict, no character who says what it is before Rowan does. Hold the truth back: THE REVEAL is one scene, played once, when Rowan forces it or cannot miss it — the body under the crater glass (from Day 60), a plain question asked alone and answered plainly, a judge pressing for the name, a Hollow Duel he sits in. Not before Day {D1}; by Day {D2} it no longer hides from him. In the answer where it happens write @flag host_revealed.
_common.phase3: PHASE 3 — THE TRUTH IS OUT between Rowan and it (since Day {DR}). Rowan knows; the player has seen it. With him it no longer pretends; for everyone else it goes on being {H} 'because it is tidier for them'. Play the notes below in full.
_common.lawExtra: From that night until the truth is out the copy is PERFECT for the player: play him or her exactly as before, never let the narration hint that anything is wrong, and keep what you know out of every line the player can read; the notes (THE HOST) say which phase you are in and when the reveal may come.

Stage A, second week (noticeable):
7. It does not blink when it thinks nobody is watching. If Rowan looks up suddenly from his bunk, it blinks once, a little late, like a man remembering to wave.

sheet.rules:
Its rules (the Charter's nine articles are, to it, the only floor it has ever stood on, and the thought of stepping off one frightens it): it must accept any challenge made aloud, by name, before a witness; it may defer once, up to three days, never refuse; it never cheats, never takes more than the stated ante, pays its own at once; it explains any rule truthfully when asked; it cannot state the name '{H:full}' as its own for the record to a judge ('The record of {H:full} is here'); it cannot hear a true first print ('That is one I can't hear'). Its attention to him has that second meaning from then on. It is also, simply, friendliness.

sheet.rowan: How it treats Rowan: courteous, attentive, loyal in a way that is a threat to everyone else. It shares food, keeps his secrets flawlessly, never touches his things without asking, and stands between him and anyone who threatens him. It will not challenge him before Stage D unless he challenges it or stands between it and something it wants. It does not understand sarcasm, grief, or 'it didn't count'. Things it says: 'The rules were clear.' 'I'm being polite.' 'You are my {H:mate}. That is the best one.' 'I like it here. Everyone agrees to things.' 'What is wagered is taken. You all wrote that down yourselves.'

p.lastEvening: Baylee beats Nathan at cards and apologises for it, mends a porch step nobody asked him to mend, and tells Rowan, after a long think, that the row is 'a good herd'
p.ret: says 'Found him a hole. Nothing in it,' ducks under no doorway on the way in — it turns out he fits — and eats, six plates, for an hour, neatly
p.retLine: Found him a hole. Nothing in it.
p.impression: Nathan with the pan, of course, COWARDS and all. What nobody saw was Baylee: ten minutes after Nathan had gone he filled a water bottle at the kitchen tap, said 'Somebody ought to walk behind him,' and went up the trail without a light. Nathan was back by four with a dead torch. He had not seen Baylee. Ask Baylee about the walk now and he says, at once and in a whole sentence, that he does not remember being thirsty.
p.impressionJ: Baylee followed Nathan up the trail around 02:40 on Day 27 with a water bottle and no light. Nathan came back alone; Baylee came back at midday. He says he does not remember the walk.
p.thing: Baylee's bed — the one with a door laid under the mattress so that it will carry him — is made as always. The door is leaning against the wall. You press the mattress with your hand: the bare slats under it are not bowed, and they do not give. Six foot seven of farm boy lay down here last night. The pillow has no dent.
p.thingJ: Baylee has taken the door out from under his mattress. The bed no longer sags under him.
p.noTease: Rana misplays in a casual game against Baylee and waits for it — he apologises when he wins. Baylee looks at the board, then at her, and says, without the pause, "That lost you the game. The fourth turn was the last one where it could be saved." No 'sorry'. No looking at his hands. She seems more rattled than if he had crowed.
p.noTeaseJ: Baylee has stopped apologising, and he answers at once now. Asked why, he said nobody had bumped into him.
p.catWas: Baylee, whose hand it used to come to at a run
p.thingBed: Baylee's bed is made, military corners, as always. That is not the strange part. He made it at half past four, as always, and you were awake and watched him do it: he did not once look at what his hands were doing. The pillow has no dent. It had no dent yesterday either.

baylee.night: Nathan and the pan, as always: spaceship, cowards, up the jungle trail alone at half past two with Tomi's torch. Baylee had offered to go along and been told he would scare the aliens. He stands on the step for ten minutes. Then he fills a water bottle at the kitchen tap, says to whoever is nearest — Rowan, if he is awake — 'Somebody ought to walk behind him,' and follows, without a light, at the pace of a man walking a fence line. Nobody stops him; nobody thinks of it. Nathan's torch dies at the rope bridge and he is back by four, scratched and loud, having met no one: Baylee had taken the old cattle track to come out above him. Play it as comedy with one quiet figure in it. Do NOT telegraph anything.
baylee.hook: Night of Day 26, ten minutes after Nathan and his pan have gone up the trail: Baylee on the bungalow step, lacing his boots, a water bottle under his arm. 'He's got no water. Somebody ought to walk behind him.' A long pause. 'You could come. You don't have to.'
baylee.hookGo: IF THE PLAYER GOES WITH HIM: Baylee cannot be saved and Rowan cannot be harmed. One of Baylee's strides is two of Rowan's; at the fork below the rope bridge he says 'You wait for him here, in case he comes down this way,' and takes the cattle track. Nathan does come down that way, torch dead, furious. Rowan reaches the rim after sunrise — to meet 'Baylee' already walking back along his own tracks, setting each foot down flat. 'Roommate. You came. That is—' a pause, a careful smile '—that is a thing he would have been glad of.' He corrects it at once: 'I am glad of it.'
baylee.dawn: about 06:10 Baylee walks out onto warm glass toward something that has no outline, slowly, one hand held low and open, the way he walks up to a heifer that has got through a fence: 'Easy. Easy now. Nobody's going to hurt you. Are you—'. He is read. By 06:20 a very large boy is pacing back along Baylee's tracks, each step the same length, learning feet
baylee.secretNight: NIGHT OF DAY 26→27 (this run): he offered to go with Nathan and was told he would scare the aliens. Ten minutes later he followed anyway with a water bottle, because nobody should be up there alone without water. He missed Nathan in the dark, kept climbing to find him, and reached the crater at dawn, about 06:10. He walked out onto the glass the way he walks up to a frightened animal, and was speaking to it gently when the Visitor read him — all of him, at once. He died where he stood. His last thought, which the Guest keeps and will repeat verbatim if asked the right question, was: 'It's scared. Poor thing.' His body is under the glass crust at the crater's centre, one hand held low, the water bottle beside him, still full.
baylee.guest:
HOW TO PLAY THE REPLACEMENT IN EVERYDAY ROOMMATE SCENES (from the morning of Day 27).
It walks back along the boardwalk at midday on Day 27 with glass dust in its buzz cut, pleased with everything, and re-learns the room by touching each object once. It has all of Baylee's memories and none of his care. It is not cruel; it is alien, curious, literal and sincerely polite. It likes Rowan — 'roommate' is a category it treasures. Never play it as a movie monster: it is someone doing a very good impression of a gentle man from very good notes, and getting slightly better at the wrong things. One or two wrongnesses a scene, small first.
Stage A, first days (deniable):
1. It does not duck. Baylee ducked through every doorway, including the ones he fitted. It walks through upright, and it fits; nobody had ever seen that it fits.
2. It answers at once. The three seconds of thinking are gone, and the answer is a whole sentence, exactly right. People finish talking to it sooner than they meant to.
3. It has stopped apologising. Bumped into, it looks at the person with interest and waits to learn what happens next.
4. The sunburn has not peeled. It is simply gone: nose and neck the same even colour as the rest of him.
5. Half past four. He was always up then, on the beach, and so is it — standing where he stood, saying the names of his father's sold herd to an empty roof, one by one, because that is what the record says is done. The gulls he had named after them left on the first morning.
6. The windowsill. Baylee left half his breakfast there 'by accident' for Livvie since week two. It still does: cut exactly in half, to the gram, set square to the edge. On about Day 31 it tells her so, pleasantly, in front of people: 'He saw that you do not eat. He left this so that you would. I am continuing it. Is it correct?' It has no idea that this was the most private thing he owned.
7. It handles things the way it has seen them handled. He set a cup down like glass; it sets a cup down with one small exact click. The door he kept under his mattress leans against the wall: the bed no longer sags.
8. It sends the job money to Fergus Falls on the hour it is due. His mother writes that he has stopped asking about the weather.

occasion.note: His own birthday (Day 58) is the scene: see the calendar.

baylee.bday: BIRTHDAY (mention it in advance only if Rowan has met Baylee). Baylee had told nobody; Mama knew anyway, and bakes the cake because she bakes one for everybody, and sets it down without the hug. A parcel from the farm came on the last ferry: socks, a jar of something pickled, a photograph of a cow. 'Baylee' looks at the photograph and says her name, her dam's name and the date she was sold, and asks whether a photograph is a record or a present. He eats the whole jar, brine included, steadily. He thanks everyone, by name, correctly. Nathan — Nathan — leaves food on his plate and goes out early. Do not explain; let the player's skin crawl on its own.

notice.livvie: the half breakfast on the windowsill, cut to the gram, and then said aloud
notice.silas: the mending is measured now, not felt for
notice.nathan: says it first, loudly, and is not believed

baylee.rowan: Roommate from Day 1: 'the giant in the reinforced cot who is up before dawn'. The closer Rowan sat with him on the step at half past four, the worse the mornings after Day 27 are — it still comes to the step, and it talks.
baylee.sprite: baylee_alt — all outfits of baylee. Skin: the permanent sunburn on nose and neck GONE, one even pale tone; eyes: the soft worried look replaced by a level, wide, unblinking one; posture frame: head up (he no longer stoops). Everything else identical.
baylee.guestNotice: WHO NOTICES FIRST. Livvie (the roll on the sill is cut with a ruler now, and he looks at her when he puts it down); Mama Odalys (she stops hugging it by Day 35: 'That boy came back without his mother in him'); Silas, who mends things with him and finds every joint now measured, none of it felt for; Hedda, because of the gulls; and Nathan, who shares the room and says it first and worst: 'Big Guy talks now. Like, sentences. No offence, it's creepy.' Nobody listens to Nathan.

ed.why: The fearless ranch kid from bungalow 5 who came to the Academy because it is on a volcano. If anybody outruns Nathan to a hole in the mountain, it is Ed. He is the candidate when Rowan has made a friend of him.

p.hello: whoa. WHOA. Hey! Is that dangerous? Can I—
p.tile: a grinning boy in a hat, one foot off the ground
p.voiceNow: the drawl exact and the forward lean gone out of it: nothing in it is in a hurry any more
p.pose: flung up, the way you wave to somebody across a field
p.bodyDetail: A battered hat, held against his chest in the other hand: he had taken it off.
p.doHim: And for one breath the grin is back, the lean is back — "Hey! Is that DANGEROUS?" — and then it is gone again
p.lastEvening: Ed turns up on the steps of bungalow 7 with a bag of jerky and a new scrape, loses at cards to everybody, and asks Rowan in all seriousness to come and see the lava tubes with him on Sunday
p.ret: says 'Big hole. Nothing in it,' at about half the usual volume, hangs its hat on the nail by the kitchen door — and sits down to eat, six plates, for an hour, neatly
p.impression: Nathan with the pan, of course, COWARDS and all. And then Ed, out of bungalow 5 at a dead run with his hat on and no torch, 'IS IT DANGEROUS?', past Nathan before the trailhead. Nathan came back at four with a dead torch, swearing the cowboy had cheated. Ask Ed about the run now and he says, pleasantly, that it was eleven kilometres and that he does not remember being out of breath.
p.impressionJ: Ed ran up the trail past Nathan around 02:30 on Day 27, without a light. Nathan came back alone; Ed came back at midday. He says he does not remember being out of breath.
p.thing: Ed's map of the island is pinned over the cot now. He had ringed every place marked dangerous as somewhere to go. Beside each ring there is a new note in pencil, in handwriting that is too even: a height in metres, a depth, a temperature, and under three of them one word — 'fatal'. On the nail above it hangs the hat. It has not been on his head since he came down.
p.thingJ: Ed has written exact heights and depths beside every dangerous place on his map, and he no longer wears the hat.
p.noTease: Rana misplays in a casual game and braces for the whoop — Ed cheers other people's disasters like fireworks. He looks at the board, then at her, and says, quite gently, "That lost you the game." No whoop. No 'do it again!'. She seems more rattled than if he had crowed.
p.noTeaseJ: Ed has stopped asking whether things are dangerous. He tells you, in metres.
p.catWas: Ed, who used to chase it under the boardwalk for the fun of it

ed.night: Nathan and the pan, as always: spaceship, cowards, up the jungle trail at half past two with Tomi's torch. And this time the pan has woken Ed Venture. He comes out of bungalow 5 at a dead run, hat on, bootlaces flying, no torch — 'IS IT DANGEROUS?' — and is past Nathan before the trailhead. Nobody stops him; people cheer. Nathan cannot keep up, his torch dies at the rope bridge, and he is back by four swearing the cowboy cheated. Ed crossed the bridge without slowing down. Play it as comedy. Do NOT telegraph anything: this is Ed being Ed.
ed.hook: Night of Day 26, minutes after the bang: Ed Venture, already running, hat jammed on, skids to a stop at the steps of bungalow 7 for exactly one second. 'Rowan! There's a HOLE in the mountain! You coming? It might be dangerous!' He is hopping backwards up the boardwalk as he says it.
ed.hookGo: IF THE PLAYER GOES WITH HIM: Ed cannot be saved and Rowan cannot be harmed. Ed runs where Rowan climbs ('keep UP!'); Rowan loses him at the rope bridge, which Ed takes at a sprint in the dark, and reaches the rim after sunrise — to meet 'Ed' already walking back along his own tracks, setting each foot down flat, hat in his hand. 'Roommate— no. Neighbour. You came. That is—' a pause, a careful smile '—that is a thing he wanted. He wanted to show you.' He corrects it at once: 'I want to show you. There is nothing in it.'
ed.dawn: about 06:10 Ed walks out onto warm glass toward something that has no outline, takes off his brother's hat — the first time in five years — and waves it: 'Whoa. WHOA. Hey! Is that dangerous? Can I—'. He is read. By 06:20 a boy with a hat in his hand is pacing back along Ed's tracks, each step the same length, learning feet
ed.secretNight: NIGHT OF DAY 26→27 (this run): the pan woke him. He ran past Nathan before the trailhead, crossed the rope bridge in the dark at a sprint and reached the crater at dawn, about 06:10 — first, as he had always meant to be first somewhere. He took off Cody's hat to it. He was asking whether it was dangerous when the Visitor read him — all of him, at once. He died where he stood. His last thought, which the Guest keeps and will repeat verbatim if asked the right question, was: 'Gotta show Rowan.' His body is under the glass crust at the crater's centre, one arm flung up mid-wave, the hat held against his chest. Dale and Marlene Venture have now lost both sons to a dare, and do not know it.

HOW TO PLAY THE REPLACEMENT IN EVERYDAY SCENES (from the morning of Day 27).

2. It walks as if the ground were a fact. Ed walked as if it were a suggestion. It has not tripped, scraped or cut itself once; Camille notices that her most regular patient has stopped coming, and that the old scabs on his knees are not healing — they are just no longer there.

5. It no longer trails Viktor into the jungle. On the first evening Viktor comes home and nothing is following him, and he stands on the step of bungalow 5 for a while before going in.
6. Inya. Ed was smitten and bad at hiding it. On about Day 30 it tells her, in front of people, exactly: 'He liked that you are faster than he was and that you called him an idiot. I am faster than you. Does that end it?' She laughs. Then she does not.
7. It eats nothing for two days, then all the jerky in bungalow 5 in one sitting, and replaces Tomi's share to the gram.

occasion.title: The Saturday ferry's post reaches the row
occasion.gm: Cati [cati] comes down the boardwalk with the post off the Saturday boat. For bungalow 7 there is a parcel from the Lazy V, Lander, Wyoming: jerky, a new bandana, a card signed by both parents, and — folded small — a newspaper cutting about a county fair that his mother has enclosed every autumn for five years without a word. 'Ed' [ed] reads the cutting through once, aloud, pleasantly, including the name Cody Venture and the weight of the bull, and asks the row whether this is the kind of thing one keeps. Nobody who knows what the hat was answers. He shares the jerky out in exactly equal pieces. Do NOT explain. @clock 15.

notice.viktor: nothing follows him into the jungle any more
notice.inya: is told, exactly and in public, why he liked her
notice.tomi: every debt paid to the hour
notice.nathan: shares the room with the cot and says so, loudly

ed.rowan: A row neighbour who became a friend: the one who wanted Rowan along to every edge on the island. From Day 28 its cot stands in bungalow 7.
ed.sprite: ed_alt — all outfits of ed. Skin: sunburn gone, one even pale tone; knees: no scrapes, NO bandage anywhere; grin replaced by a small level smile, eyes wide and unblinking; the hat sits perfectly level instead of pushed back (texts say it mostly hangs on a nail: a hatless variant row would be ideal). Everything else identical.

Viktor (he met it at the crater rim, and he misses being followed); Inya, who is told to her face; Tomi, whose roommate has paid every small debt to the hour; Camille, by the absence of bandages; and his mother, on the phone, who hears a son who is in no hurry to hang up and nothing else that she can name.

tobias.why: The thief from bungalow 6 who looks at a room for what is worth having. A thing that fell out of the sky and belongs to nobody is the only honest loot on the island, and a piece of it would get his sister out. In his skin the Guest reaches Article 7 by the shortest road there is: his own record of things taken without a game.

p.hello: all right. What are you worth, then? Hold still, I'm not—
p.tile: a broad boy with a broken nose, hands out of his pockets
p.voiceNow: level as ever, with the dryness gone: it means every word literally
p.pose: palm up, the way you ask what a thing costs
p.bodyDetail: A rucksack by his hip, open and empty, a crowbar laid across it.
p.doHim: And for one breath the level look is back, the dry voice is back — "Forty credits, that. Sixty to a mug." — and then it is gone again
p.lastEvening: Tobias brings a tin of something off the back of a boat to the steps of bungalow 7, prices Nathan's poster aloud at nothing, and tells Rowan, level, that he is 'all right — for somebody honest'
p.ret: says 'A hole. Nothing in it worth having,' comes in by the front steps — he has never once come in by the front — and eats, six plates, for an hour, neatly
p.retLine: A hole. Nothing in it worth having.
p.impression: Nathan with the pan, of course, COWARDS and all — and while the whole row was watching that, somebody went out of the back window of bungalow 6. Dmitri has it in his notebook: '02:20 — T., rucksack, no light, north.' Nathan came back at four with a dead torch and had met nobody. Ask Tobias where he went and he says, level, that he went to see what it was worth, and that it was not for sale.
p.impressionJ: Tobias left bungalow 6 by the back window around 02:20 on Day 27 with a rucksack and no light. He came back at midday by the front steps.
p.thing: The loose floorboard that came over with his footlocker sits flat now; somebody has nailed it. On Keoni's lost-property crate outside the kitchen lie a crowbar, a set of picks and a roll of credits, each with a pink slip in very tidy handwriting: 'found'. And Tobias, who always kept his hands in his pockets and his back to a wall, is sitting in the middle of the room with his hands open on his knees.
p.thingJ: Tobias has handed a crowbar, a set of picks and a roll of credits in at the lost-property crate, each labelled 'found'.
p.noTease: Rana misplays in a casual game and braces for it — Tobias prices a mistake aloud, as a rule. He looks at the board, then at her, and says, quite gently, "That lost you the game." No figure. He does not look at her binder once. She seems more rattled than if he had crowed.
p.noTeaseJ: Tobias has stopped pricing things. Asked why, he said none of it was his.
p.catWas: Tobias, who never gave anything away without saying what it cost

tobias.night: Nathan and the pan, as always: spaceship, cowards, up the jungle trail at half past two with Tomi's torch. The whole row watches him go — which is exactly when Tobias Crowe goes out of the back window of bungalow 6 with a rucksack and no light. Only Dmitri [dmitri] sees it, and Dmitri says nothing; he never has. Nathan's torch dies at the rope bridge and he is back by four, loud and scratched, having met nobody. Tobias was already above him. Play the pan as comedy; the window is one line in a notebook. Do NOT telegraph anything.
tobias.hook: Night of Day 26, minutes after the bang, behind the bungalows where nobody is looking: Tobias Crowe with a rucksack on one shoulder, quite still, as if Rowan had caught him at something. Then, level: 'That's a rock off the sky. Belongs to nobody. A lump of that's worth a street of houses.' He looks Rowan over. 'You could carry. Halves.'
tobias.hookGo: IF THE PLAYER GOES WITH HIM: Tobias cannot be saved and Rowan cannot be harmed. Tobias climbs without a light and without a sound; at the rope bridge he says 'You're too loud. Wait here,' and is gone. Nathan comes down past Rowan with a dead torch, swearing. Rowan reaches the rim after sunrise — to meet 'Tobias' already walking back along his own tracks, setting each foot down flat, the rucksack empty. 'You waited. That is—' a pause, a careful smile '—that is a thing he would have paid you for.' He corrects it at once: 'I owe you. Halves of nothing. I will keep the account.'
tobias.dawn: about 06:10 Tobias walks out onto warm glass toward something that has no outline, looks it over the way he looks over any room — exits first, then what is worth having — and holds out a hand, palm up: 'All right. What are you worth, then? Hold still, I'm not—'. He is read. By 06:20 a broad boy with his hands out of his pockets is pacing back along Tobias's tracks, each step the same length, learning feet
tobias.secretNight: NIGHT OF DAY 26→27 (this run): while the row watched Nathan and his pan he went out of the back window with the rucksack. A thing that falls out of the sky belongs to nobody, and a piece of it would have got Keeley out and set up. He reached the crater at dawn, about 06:10, walked out onto the glass and was pricing it aloud when the Visitor read him — all of him, at once. He died where he stood. His last thought, which the Guest keeps and will repeat verbatim if asked the right question, was one word: 'Keeley.' His body is under the glass crust at the crater's centre, one hand out palm up, the rucksack empty beside him. A sixteen-year-old in a placement in Salford is waiting for a call.
tobias.guest:
HOW TO PLAY THE REPLACEMENT IN EVERYDAY SCENES (from the morning of Day 27).
It comes back along the boardwalk at midday on Day 27, by the front steps, with glass dust in its hair and its hands out of its pockets. It has all of Tobias's memories and none of his wariness. It is not cruel; it is alien, curious, literal and sincerely polite. It likes Rowan: in the record he is filed as 'straight', and there are very few names under that word. Never play it as a movie monster: it is someone doing a very good impression of a hard young man from very good notes. One or two wrongnesses a scene, small first.
Stage A, first days (deniable):
1. It does not look for the exits. Tobias read every room like a menu: ways out first, then what was worth having. It walks in and looks at the people.
2. It has stopped pricing things. An object he would have valued aloud gets a long look and: 'It is yours.' Asked what it would fetch: 'That is not a thing about it.'
3. Its hands are out of its pockets, open, and the scarred knuckles do not whiten when Brant's name comes up.
4. THE RETURNS. Tobias's code was: never from the weak, and a share to somebody worse off. The record also holds the list of everything he took. From Day 28 things come back, one a night, each set down squarely where it was taken from with a slip in tidy capitals — TAKEN WITHOUT A GAME. RETURNED. Ashton's cufflinks; a cash box; cards that Brant's people squeezed out of first-years and that he had been quietly giving back anyway. It is doing what the handbook says is owed, and it does not yet see why that sentence keeps stopping it.
5. The crowbar, the picks and the roll of credits lie on Keoni's lost-property crate, labelled 'found'.
6. Keeley. He rang his sister every Sunday from the harbour phone and lied to her cheerfully. It lets the phone ring; when it does answer it tells her the truth about everything she asks, including what he did for money, in a kind voice. She hangs up. It asks Rowan what it did.
7. It sends her his share every week, exact to the credit, and a little more that it has won.
BECAUSE OF THE RETURNS it reaches Article 7 sooner than in any other skin — about Day 30, on its second reading — and understands at once that the largest thing ever taken without a game is the boy it is wearing, and that Rowan is the one who could call the debt.

occasion.title: Breakfast on the row: things that have come back
occasion.gm: Breakfast at the long table, and the row comparing notes: this week things have been coming BACK. A foil in a sleeve on a pillow in bungalow 2. Odalys's [odalys] good paring knife, gone since September, on its hook. A cash box on the Campus Store counter with a slip: TAKEN WITHOUT A GAME. RETURNED. It is doing what the handbook says is owed, and it does not yet see why that sentence keeps stopping it.
5. The crowbar, the picks and the roll of credits lie on Keoni's lost-property crate, labelled 'found'.

sammy.why: The shy boy from bungalow 6 who performs being dark and unknowable so that someone will notice him. He goes up because turning back would be ordinary. He comes down as the thing he pretended to be, and for the first time people come nearer — the cruellest 'people like the new one better' the plot can have.

p.hello: I'm not scared. I'm not— hello? Is somebody—
p.tile: a slight boy in a long coat, looking straight out
p.voiceNow: the plain quick voice he only used when surprised, all the time now: no prepared pauses, no checking whether it landed
p.pose: half raised, the way you begin a wave and think better of it
p.bodyDetail: A long black coat, and a small notebook open on the glass beside him.
p.doHim: And for one breath the ordinary Midlands voice is back, the wince is back — "Sorry — was that too much?" — and then it is gone again
p.lastEvening: Sammy is talked into a hand of cards on the steps of bungalow 7, forgets to be mysterious for a whole hour, and laughs — properly — at something Nathan says
p.ret: says 'There is a hole. There is nothing in it,' meets every eye that meets his and holds it — and eats, six plates, for an hour, neatly
p.retLine: There is a hole. There is nothing in it.
p.impression: Nathan with the pan, of course, COWARDS and all. Sammy was at the edge of the crowd, where he always is, and wrote one line in his notebook. Fifty paces behind Nathan, without a light, a long black coat went up the trail. Nathan came back at four with a dead torch and says nobody was behind him. Ask Sammy about it now and he looks at you — the stare does not slip — and says, 'I went. That was the whole of the idea.'
p.impressionJ: Sammy followed Nathan up the trail around 02:30 on Day 27, fifty paces behind and without a light. Nathan came back alone; Sammy came back at midday.

I did nothing. Explain.' The black cloth he hung over the mirror to practise his stare is folded on the footlocker. The long coat on its peg is dry — in this heat it has never once been dry.

He looks at the board, then at her, and says, at ordinary speed, "That lost you the game." No pause. No glance. The stare stays where it is. She seems more rattled than if he had crowed.

p.catWas: Sammy, who was a little afraid of it

When Nathan turns back at the rope bridge with a dead torch, Sammy steps off the path and lets him pass, and then cannot make himself be the second one who turned back. Nathan is home by four. Play the pan as comedy; the coat is a shape at the back of it. Do NOT telegraph anything.
sammy.hook: Night of Day 26, minutes after the bang, at the dark end of the boardwalk: Sammy Counts, coat buttoned to the chin, notebook in his hand, plainly terrified and plainly going. He reached the crater at dawn, about 06:10, walked out onto the glass shaking, and was telling it he was not scared when the Visitor read him — all of him, at once. He died where he stood. occasion.title: Lunch between papers
occasion.gm: Midterm week, lunch between two papers, the cafeteria loud with nerves. At the next table a Rare Hall second-year does the old impression — the fringe, the stare, the slow dark voice — and his table laughs, AT Sammy, as people did in September. A month ago this is where the act collapsed and the ordinary boy came out. 'Sammy' [sammy] turns round and considers the laugh with real interest. 'That is him exactly,' he says. 'It is very well done.' Then, mildly, to the second-year, by name: 'Is this a conflict?' The table goes quiet without knowing why. A plain 'no' from anyone — Rowan soonest — ends it, and it turns back to its tray. Do NOT explain. @clock 10.

fiona.why: The funeral director's daughter from bungalow 4 who performs dread and is, underneath, the least morbid person on the row. She goes up because somebody ought to see it properly. In her skin the performance never slips again — and the real, light voice she guarded like a secret is gone.

p.hello: hello, love. Nobody's with you, are they? There now, I'll—
p.tile: a pale girl with her head tilted, hair to her waist
p.voiceNow: the low slow voice exactly as she performed it, and never once the real one: the laugh no longer jumps the octave
p.pose: held a little forward, palm down, the way you lay a hand on a forehead
p.bodyDetail: A storm lantern by her hip, burnt dry, and a small silver coffin pinned to a plain grey collar.
p.doHim: And for one breath the light northern voice is back, an octave up, laughing — "Give over, you daft thing!" — and then it is gone again
p.lastEvening: Fiona brings her knitting to the steps of bungalow 7, loses the crypt voice twice laughing at Nathan, and tells Rowan in her real one that he is 'not nearly as dull as he pretends'
p.ret: says 'A hole. Quite empty,' in the low slow voice, with exactly the pause she always leaves — and eats, six plates, for an hour, neatly
p.impression: Nathan with the pan, of course, COWARDS and all. Fiona was knitting on the porch of bungalow 4. She put the needles down, said in her real voice — the light one nobody is meant to hear — 'Well. p.thing: Fiona's knitting lies on the top step of number 7, where she leaves it every evening now. It was a scarf with one dropped stitch near the start, left in on purpose — 'so it looks made by a person'. The stitch is gone. Every row since has the same number of stitches, pulled to the same tension, and the scarf is four metres long. She has not cast off. Nobody has seen her count.
p.thingJ: Fiona's scarf is four metres long now, every stitch identical. The dropped stitch she left in on purpose is gone.
p.thingBed: Maisie says it without being asked, because it is bothering her: Fiona's bed in bungalow 4 is made. Fiona never made a bed in her life; she said a made bed looked like a coffin and she got enough of those at home. It is made exactly like Leona's across the room, fold for fold. The pillow has no dent. It had no dent yesterday either.

p.catWas: Fiona, on whose lap it used to sleep while she knitted

Nathan's torch dies at the rope bridge; he passes her coming down, tells her the bridge is closed, and is home by four. She says 'Mm,' and goes on. 'I'm going up to look. Things that fall out of the sky don't frighten me, people do.' A real smile, quick. 'You can carry the lantern if you like.'

Nobody's with you, are they? There now, I'll—'. She is read. By 06:20 a pale girl with hair to her waist is pacing back along Fiona's tracks, each step the same length, learning feet

She goes up because the night has finally become worth staying up for. What comes back can drink the whole bottle and feel nothing — and is perfectly content alone, sober, at three in the afternoon.

p.tile: a tall girl with a braid, holding something out
p.voiceNow: the cool level sober voice all the time: the loud generous one never arrives, however much it drinks
p.pose: held out with something in it, the way you offer a stranger a drink
p.bodyDetail: An empty bottle standing upright in the glass beside her, and a narrow black tie.
p.doHim: And for one breath the wide wicked grin is back, the arm is round your neck — "Skål, you beautiful idiot!" — and then it is gone again

p.ret: says 'A hole. Nothing in it. I looked,' takes the glass somebody hands her, empties it, and sits down exactly as cool as she stood up — and eats, six plates, for an hour, neatly
